correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs component hypotheses including strict winding boundaries, uses the exact published good cover to determine the primitive e0 image (2Z for odd n and Z for even n), proves adjacent coordinate evaluations homotopic, and deduces every integral group-generator sign by e0 injectivity. The quotient argument uses exact rational finite-group coinvariants. Actual bundled checkers independently confirm evaluation indices and all 452 small group-element trace tests. Finite runs are supporting checks, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The accepted claim is the exact integral D_m x D_n signed permutation module and evaluation-index dichotomy, not the earlier circle-or-point classification. Primary full-text statements and the published good-cover proof were compared by implication. An indexed-record similarity search and targeted mathematical literature searches found no result stating or implying the complete module; inaccessible/unindexed works remain residual priority risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent unindexed thesis, preprint, dissertation or unpublished calculation may exist.
The full Babson–Kozlov foundational monograph/article was not inspected for every possible variant; its indexed abstract and declared target families were used only as limited evidence.
The cycle-codomain paper of Fujii and coauthors uses a concrete universal cover whose full equivariant behavior might support an equivalent derivation; no covering statement was identified.
The new theorem specializes familiar published homotopy methods, so priority of this exact equivariant refinement warrants independent literature assessment.

value.rationale: For a canonical two-parameter family with known nonequivariant homotopy, the exact integral D_m x D_n representation is an intrinsic symmetry invariant not implied by rank. The structural classification is motivated by topological graph colorings and component symmetries, not arbitrary finite sampling.
